4.1 — The Enemy: Waypoint Patrols

The turret never moves; the enemy hunts. Start with its calmest behavior: a guard walking a beat, back and forth, forever — a loop built from one saved position and one sign flip.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the patrol half of EnemyController.cs:

[SerializeField] private float speed = 2.0f;
[SerializeField] private float patrolDistance = 3.0f;
private Vector3 startPosition;
private int direction = 1;

private void Start()
{
    startPosition = transform.position;
    ...
}

private void PlatformerMove()
{
    transform.Translate(Vector2.right * direction * speed * Time.deltaTime);

    float dist = Vector3.Distance(startPosition, transform.position);
    if (dist > patrolDistance)
    {
        direction *= -1; // Switch direction
        ...
    }
}

Predict before running: the enemy starts at x = 5. Where does it turn around — at x = 8, x = 2, or both? Draw the walk as a line with turn-around points. Then: why does Start save startPosition — what would break if Update saved it instead?

Socratic

The patrol is a loop with no loop keyword — Translate every frame, flip when far. Where is the "repeat" hiding, and what would the AP exam's REPEAT UNTIL version of this look like?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — rebuild the patrol from a blank EnemyController. Comment out PlatformerMove's body and bring it back in order: remember start (Start) → walk (Translate with direction × speed × deltaTime — the movement pattern from 1.4, wearing a sign) → measure (Distance from start) → flip (direction *= -1). Run after each step; the walk is boring alone, the flip is the behavior.

Step 2 — the invisible leash. There are no markers in the scene — no waypoint gizmos, nothing. The enemy patrols relative to where it spawned: move the prefab instance in the scene and the beat moves too. patrolDistance is the leash length, a serialized knob like every other. What is the patrol shape if you set patrolDistance to 0? To 100?

Step 3 — direction as signed state. A single int, 1 or −1, is the enemy's entire memory of where it is going. Multiplying by −1 flips the sign — one line, no ifs. This is the trick behind every "which way am I facing" field in games; your sprite.flipX from 4.2 reads this exact value.

Bug Hunt: The runaway guard

  1. Move the enemy mid-patrol in the Scene view while in PLAY mode. What is its new turnaround pattern, and why does it never find its old beat?
  2. Save startPosition in Update instead of Start. The enemy... what? Explain using the value startPosition holds on frame 2.
  3. Change direction *= -1 to direction = 1. What single behavior remains — and where does the enemy end up after ten seconds?
  4. Set speed to 20 and watch a full beat. Which side of the leash does the flip overshoot — and why does a big speed make the patrol longer than patrolDistance?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Design the beat

  1. Place two enemies with overlapping patrols guarding a coin. Where do the beats intersect, and can the player time the gap?
  2. Patrol on ONE axis only, by code. What would you change to make a vertical guard (an elevator enemy)?
  3. Hard: a patrol that pauses at each end for one second. Which pattern from 3.3 do you reach for — and what is the "cooldown" here?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Rebuild the patrol: save start → translate → measure → flip
  • Explain why Start saves the anchor and Update cannot
  • Explain direction as signed state and the *= −1 flip
  • Design patrol layouts (overlaps, leashes, choke points) on purpose
